items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: As a matter of fact one of them was "Muttin Leg" Mudden-Leg, with Illinois Jacquet Jacquet, and his orchestra.

ctx.x: They were very responsive, but he -- Panassi Panaci had enough seats there to kind of disrupt things for her, you know, for a while. But this is how fanatical they were about this. And it was kind of nice seeing Kenny because I had recorded with these, I guess they're all stars at that time. When I came out of the army. This was done in '46. This was called 52nd Street jazz, I believe, and this was a original recording of Kenny's tune "Epistrophy." And in the band was Fats Novarro Navarro, Kenny Durham Durham,…

And as I say, it was the first time I had seen Kenny since then, and during that time as I told you I did so many recordings with Jacquet Jacquet and Dizzy also. As a matter of fact one of them was "Muttin Leg" Mudden-Leg, with Illinois Jacquet Jacquet, and his orchestra. And in that band was Leo Parker and Sir Charles

Thompson, Joe Newman and Russell Jacquet, and J. J. Johnson, Al Lucas on bass on -- Shadow Wilson on drum, which was quite 'Ow' 'Oo Pop A Dum' a band. And I know that I did Owi and Ooh-Bopadomp, with Dizzy, yeah. And let's see, who was in this band. David Elman Burns, Simon Wright and Matthew McKay and Ray Orr was trumpet. Howard Johnson and John Brown, alto sax, and James Moore Moody and Joe Gales, tenor sax. Cecil Payne was in the band, baritone. And John Lewis, piano, Ray Brown, bass, Milt Jackson and Joe…
